gunditjmara.name: Gunditjmara
gunditjmara.summary: An Aboriginal people of southwestern Victoria, Australia, known for engineering extensive eel aquaculture systems and for their resistance to British invasion in the Eumeralla Wars.

budj-bim.name: Budj Bim
budj-bim.summary: Dormant volcano, also called Mount Eccles, in southwestern Victoria, Australia, whose lava flows created wetlands that the Gunditjmara used for eel farming.

bush-tucker.name: Bush tucker
bush-tucker.summary: Native Australian foods historically eaten by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, including kangaroo, emu, and native fruits and yams.

lake-condah.name: Lake Condah
lake-condah.summary: A shallow lake in Victoria, Australia, also known by its Gunditjmara name Tae Rak, where local Aboriginal people built extensive eel-trapping and aquaculture systems.

budj-bim-heritage-areas.name: Budj Bim wetlands
budj-bim-heritage-areas.summary: Protected volcanic landscape in Victoria, Australia, shaped by the eruption of Budj Bim more than 30,000 years ago, including Lake Condah where the Gunditjmara built an extensive aquaculture system up to 8,000 years old.

acacia-melanoxylon.name: Australian blackwood
acacia-melanoxylon.summary: An Acacia tree species native to southeastern Australia, also called blackwood or hickory, now invasive elsewhere.

flandrian-interglacial.name: Flandrian transgression
flandrian-interglacial.summary: A period of rapid sea-level rise around 12,000 years ago at the start of the current interglacial, caused by melting glaciers, which flooded glacial valleys to form fjords.

eucalyptus-gunnii.name: Cider gum
eucalyptus-gunnii.summary: A small to medium-sized flowering tree species with white flowers, whose sap (manna) was used by Aboriginal Tasmanians to make a syrup or an alcoholic cider.

arnhem-land.name: Arnhem Land
arnhem-land.summary: A remote region of Australia's Northern Territory, named after a Dutch ship in 1623 and home mostly to Aboriginal Australians, many living in small communities with little Western influence.

sydney-sandstone.name: Sydney sandstone
sydney-sandstone.summary: A sedimentary rock forming the bedrock of much of Sydney, long favoured as a building material and the reason many Aboriginal carvings there survive.

ku-ring-gai-council.name: Ku-ring-gai Council
ku-ring-gai-council.summary: Local government area in northern Sydney, Australia, named after an Aboriginal language group and containing part of Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park.

paul-ta-on.name: Paul Taçon
paul-ta-on.summary: Australia-based anthropologist and archaeologist known for major rock art discoveries, including the earliest known rock art evidence of warfare and the origins of the Rainbow Serpent motif.

george-chaloupka.name: George Chaloupka
george-chaloupka.summary: Czech-born Australian art historian and anthropologist (1932–2011), an expert on Indigenous rock art who coined the term 'Dynamic Figures' for a style he documented in Arnhem Land.

kimberley-western-australia.name: The Kimberley
kimberley-western-australia.summary: The northernmost of Western Australia's nine regions, bordered by the Indian Ocean and the Timor Sea, named in 1879 after the Earl of Kimberley.

gwion-gwion-rock-paintings.name: Gwion Gwion rock paintings
gwion-gwion-rock-paintings.summary: A tradition of ancient rock art in the Kimberley region of Western Australia depicting human figures, with most works estimated to be about 12,000 years old.

spear-thrower.name: Atlatl (spear-thrower)
spear-thrower.summary: A hand-held tool using leverage to launch a dart or spear at greater speed, with a cup or spur at the end that holds the spear's butt during the throw.

torres-strait.name: Torres Strait
torres-strait.summary: Strait between Australia and New Guinea, named after Spanish navigator Luís Vaz de Torres, who sailed through it in 1606.

josephine-flood.name: Josephine Flood
josephine-flood.summary: English-born Australian archaeologist, mountaineer, and author, born in 1936.

ghow-swamp.name: Ghow Swamp
ghow-swamp.summary: A reservoir in north-central Victoria, Australia, formed in 1923 from a former swamp and wetland, now used for irrigation.

alan-thorne.name: Alan Thorne
alan-thorne.summary: Australian anatomist (1939–2012) regarded as an authority on Aboriginal Australian origins, known for excavations at sites such as Lake Mungo and Kow Swamp.

cohuna.name: Cohuna
cohuna.summary: A town in northern Victoria, Australia, on the Murray Valley Highway about 274 kilometres north of Melbourne.

don-brothwell.name: Don Brothwell
don-brothwell.summary: British archaeologist and anthropologist (1933–2016) who specialised in human palaeoecology and environmental archaeology, described as a pioneer of archaeological science.

blue-mountains-new-south-wales.name: Blue Mountains
blue-mountains-new-south-wales.summary: A mountainous region on the western edge of Sydney, Australia, forming part of the Great Dividing Range.

baiame.name: Baiame
baiame.summary: The creator god and sky father in the Dreaming beliefs of several Aboriginal Australian peoples of southeastern Australia.

daramulum.name: Daramulum
daramulum.summary: A shapeshifting sky hero in south-east Australian Aboriginal cultures, associated with Baiame, depicted in rock art and whose voice is heard through the bullroarer.
